precepts.text: Behold, the days come, that I will send a famine in the land, not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for water, but of hearing the words of the Lord. They shall run to and fro to seek the word of the Lord, and shall not find it.
precepts.point: News read in class: NASA and private companies like SpaceX are advancing plans for a permanent human presence on the moon through the Artemis program, and Artemis 2 just launched. You can have your doubting Thomas saying it is all fake; is it fake like the planes you fly on? A clip of Elon Musk was played discussing colonizing Mars. Why does Esau the Edomite want to go to Mars? Because it is the red planet.

note.label: Religion - The False Prophet

precepts.why:
The vision is written plain “that he may run that readeth it.” Amos explains the running: “Behold, the days come, saith the Lord God, that I will send a famine in the land, not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for water, but of hearing the words of the Lord”.

There would be a famine of the word of the Lord. “And they shall wander from sea to sea, and from the north even to the east, they shall run to and fro to seek the word of the Lord, and shall not find it.” People would travel from sea to sea, running to and fro, looking for the word and not finding it.

That is what happened after Christ and the disciples died: there was no truth being taught in the earth, nowhere. By the time of Constantine, around 325 AD, you had the churches, and there was no truth there; they were worshiping idols. Some of the Moors were Islamic, and some were black Jews following the Talmud and the Cabala. When white folks rose up it went crazy, into idolatry like you never saw: the church fathers making doctrine, and Tertullian, the devil that created the Trinity.

And they were traveling. The crusades went here and there trying to get the cup Christ drank from and to find the cross, trying to get some kind of glimpse of understanding. They ran to and fro, just as Amos said, because the word written plain in the book had nobody left to teach it.

precepts.text: Making the ephah small and the shekel great, and falsifying the balances by deceit.
precepts.point: Biblical economics aims at communal wealth so that no generation is left stuck, and Israel should deal that way with each other now.

note.label: Babylon Speaks Plainly: Venezuela and the Real WMD

precepts.why:
“When will the new moon be gone, that we may sell corn? and the sabbath, that we may set forth wheat, making the ephah small, and the shekel great, and falsifying the balances by deceit?” That is messing with the scales. It is the same spirit of deceitful balances read in Hosea 12:7, and it was spoken against us because we had mixed among the other nations and learned it from them.

Remember when Nehemiah had to curse out the merchants from the other nations because they came to sell on the sabbath. If we had all been in the spirit, would he have had to curse them out? We would not have bought, and they would not have come. They came because we were breaking the law by buying.

We should not have that spirit, but now you see who really does. One of the grand ways they falsify the balances today is with the oil: they call Venezuela's crude too heavy, while it is more profitable to them than anything else.

It reaches into the mortgage too. Interest is designed to keep you in debt and keep you broke, and the mortgage is loaded front heavy, so the first years go mostly to interest and not principal. On a 300,000 home a 30-year loan costs an extra 250,800, and instead of fixing the economy Trump talks about a 50-year mortgage, where you pay an additional 476,000 just to have a cheaper payment, and leave that debt to your wife and kids. That is the deceit. When we think of scales we think of the little scale at the fruit market, but this shows how broad that evil principle is. Edom does it first, and they excel at it.

It is not wrong to own a home; it is better than renting. But the system is broken and was never supposed to be that way. If our economics were set up by the law, we would lend to each other without usury and own our homes. Even to that extent the Lord had righteous weights, scales and balances, and that is the wisdom and understanding Deuteronomy 4:6 speaks of.

precepts.text: They that swear by the sin of Samaria and say, The manner of Beersheba liveth; even they shall fall, and never rise up again.
precepts.point: Amos says they shall fall, and never rise up again: Dan fell and never rose again as a tribe, which is why Dan is not mentioned among the tribes of the 144,000 in Revelation 7. And as Genesis 49 says, Dan is an adder in the path: look how the islands are shaped geographically, like a serpent.

note.label: Deuteronomy 33: The Blessing of Moses, Identifying the Tribes in the Last Days

precepts.why:
“They that swear by the sin of Samaria, and say, Thy god, O Dan, liveth; and, The manner of Beer–sheba liveth; even they shall fall, and never rise up again.” Dan fell and never rose again as a tribe.

That is why Dan is not mentioned among the tribes of the 144,000 in Revelation 7. It fits the blessing: Dan leaps from Bashan, the most northern part of Israel, and lands in the middle of all Israel, so Dan today is not their own tribe but is absorbed into all the other tribes, primarily Benjamin, dwelling in the Caribbean. A warlike people, a lion’s whelp, the Carib Indians who did not play; yet as a tribe they fell and never rose up again.

precepts.text: They that swear by the sin of Samaria, and say, Thy god, O Dan, liveth, shall fall, and never rise up again; the judgment on Dan's idolatry.
precepts.point: Hear the word against Dan by the prophet: they that swear by the sin of Samaria and say, thy god, O Dan, liveth, shall fall and never rise up again. Mind you, it is an idol made with hands, yet they called it living. That is why Dan has no gate among the sealed tribes in Revelation 7; Dan was discontinued as a tribe of itself and intertwined with Benjamin for the most part.

note.label: Judges 18: Dan Steals Micah's Gods and Takes Laish

precepts.why: Hear the word against Dan by the prophet: “They that swear by the sin of Samaria, and say, Thy god, O Dan, liveth; and, The manner of Beer–sheba liveth; even they shall fall, and never rise up again.” Mind you, it is an idol made with hands, Micah’s graven image and then Jeroboam’s calf, yet they called it living. That is the judgment on Dan’s idolatry: fall, and never rise up again.

precepts.text: The cheaters ask when the new moon will be gone so they can make the ephah small and the shekel great and falsify the balances.
precepts.point: The hearing ear and the seeing eye, the Lord has made both. When you battle with someone who does not understand, it is not their time; the Lord dulls the ears and closes the spiritual eyes so they cannot see or understand.

note.label: Proverbs 20: Integrity, Just Weights, and Waiting on the Lord

precepts.why:
“Divers weights, and divers measures, both of them are alike abomination to the Lord.” Two sets of weights and two measures, one to buy with and one to sell with, is cheating, and both are an abomination to him.

Amos shows the very cheating: the merchants asking “When will the new moon be gone, that we may sell corn? and the sabbath, that we may set forth wheat, making the ephah small, and the shekel great, and falsifying the balances by deceit?” They cannot wait for the holy days to pass so they can get back to business, and their business is a small ephah, a great shekel and false balances. That is divers weights and divers measures in action.

What Solomon calls an abomination is what Amos condemns in the merchants of Israel, and the Lord has not changed his mind about it.

precepts.text: Those who swear by the sin of Samaria and the way of Dan shall fall and never rise up again.
precepts.point: Jeroboam sealed the split with idolatry, making two golden calves in Bethel and Dan, ordaining a feast of his own in the eighth month, and setting up priests of the lowest people, so the northern kingdom sank deeper and deeper into idol worship. Dan fell so hard that the tribe was absorbed and left out of the sealed tribes.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“They that swear by the sin of Samaria, and say, Thy god, O Dan, liveth; and, The manner of Beer–sheba liveth; even they shall fall, and never rise up again.”

Dan was where Jeroboam set one of the golden calves, and Dan fell so hard that the tribe was absorbed. Those who swore by the sin of Samaria and the god of Dan fell and never rose up again.
